rv.q: Ms. Waller’s shape-shifting performance is itself an eerie, unforgettable marvel.
The Creeps' overly cryptic sketches and variable audience participation sequences do not cohere into a fully satisfying theatrical experience and isn't really shocking as it has been promoted.
It’s debatable whether such intellectualizations are enough to justify the alternately intriguing and frustrating 70-minute show itself.
The whole thing feels like the starting point for an exploration, not its end point.
Although Waller’s physicality is impressive, the characters seem to be living in a vacuum.
An equally funny, unsettling, and, perhaps surprisingly, empathetic solo show from Catherine Waller, The Creeps has won awards at the Hollywood Fringe, Amsterdam Fringe, and United Solo Festival...

cn.t: Waller's unsettling solo show divides critics with its atmospheric horror and demanding audience participation. While some praise its strangeness and commitment, others find it fails to fully register despite strong elements.
